title: Planning a roof replacement with confidence
excerpt: A roof replacement is easier to manage when you understand the scope, materials and finish you want before work begins.
body: When a roof has reached the end of its working life, a full replacement can be the most reliable way to restore protection and appearance. Taking time to understand the condition of the existing roof, the finish you want and the level of disruption you can manage helps the project run more smoothly. An experienced roofing team can guide you through the process and deliver a durable result tailored to your property.

title: Choosing the right flat roofing finish
excerpt: Firestone, rubber, GRP, fibreglass and felt each suit different priorities, so clear advice matters before you commit.
body: Flat roofing projects work best when the chosen system matches the property and the brief. Materials such as firestone, rubber, GRP, fibreglass and felt can all provide durable coverings when installed professionally. Understanding the look, detailing and maintenance expectations of each option helps you choose a practical finish with confidence.

title: When to arrange roofing repairs
excerpt: Minor leaks or visible wear should be dealt with promptly to protect the roof and avoid more disruptive work later on.
body: Roofing repairs are often most effective when problems are addressed early. A small leak, loose section or worn detail can affect the wider roof if left unattended. Prompt, reliable repair work helps restore the roof’s integrity, protects the property beneath and can be a practical way to extend the life of the existing roof.
